abstract: Muon-family optimizers are being paired with 4-bit training, but the cost of low-precision gradient noise under Muon has not been measured or decomposed. We measure what unbiased stochastic-rounding MXFP4 noise on all four backward GEMM operands (forward pass in BF16) costs at the end of pretraining, in 26M- and 50M-parameter decoders trained on 0.5B tokens. Every hypothesis test was preregistered, and the supplement contains a dated export of the preregistrations. Under Muon the cost is +0.0055/+0.0067 BPB at 26M and +0.0072/+0.0061 at 50M (two seeds each), the same at both sizes within the seed spread. It appears within about 250 updates and follows the current precision. A BF16 warmdown recovers 69–76% of it across sizes and horizons. Three specific timing predictions failed, including one preregistered relaxation model. Across one seed and a fitted reference curve, the BPB gap is flat from 1× to 2× tokens while the token-equivalent tax grows from 9.4% to 16.3%. Matched-noise arms, whose achieved energy we reconstruct at 0.86–1.02 of target, show that equal energy is not equal price: FP4 error costs 1.4–1.8× sampling-shaped noise and isotropic noise 3.4×. A frozen-state update probe ranks the three in both a squared and a linear form; this match is empirical. At small batch the same quantizer costs 1.6× more (one seed, descriptive). Two results are negative. An apparent 20-fold Muon/AdamW contrast at 26M did not survive a second seed. At 50M, AdamW pays a reproducible 60–70% of Muon's cost, which the probe underprices about 4-fold. A one-constant pricing law in the probe fits four 26M points within 1.44× but failed two of three valid out-of-sample tests. We correct our earlier theory: the probe's squared form measures $\operatorname{tr}(J\Sigma J^\top)$, not the quadratic model's $\operatorname{tr}(J\Sigma)$. Quantization is simulated; code, run records and provenance are released.

change_summary:
Resubmission of 6-0VuqRD6sRzLwYt, addressing the four review points. No claims were added beyond three new runs (n07, x08, q23), each preregistered before it ran.

R1, matched energy. §3 now separates the design from the achieved energy. A new table reconstructs, from the receiving runs' gradient-norm records, the injected energy of every matched arm against three targets, including the same-seed FP4 arm. Muon totals are 0.86–1.02 of target, with per-tensor scatter 0.55–1.61. The AdamW arms got about 0.5 of the Muon-derived absolute target (q01's relative dose; 1.2× AdamW's own FP4 energy). They are now descriptive, and the AdamW structure ratios are not established. New arm n07 extends the injection to the non-matrix groups FP4 perturbs: +0.00043 vs n01, negligible by its preregistered bar. §4.4 reports energy-corrected ratios (FP4/sampling 1.29–1.38 s45, 1.55–1.83 s44) and the sublinear energy exponent (0.63). The per-tensor sums and tools/energy_check.py are in the supplement.

R2, probe theory and shape factor. §5 is rewritten. The squared form measures tr(JΣJᵀ), not the equilibrium tr(JΣ) (with the reviewer's diag(1,2) counterexample), and "measures exactly" is removed. New run x08 measures the linear form P_lin ≈ tr(JΣ): it ranks the structures too (1.24, 3.27), so the ranking is stated as empirical (1 of 6 label permutations passes). All Muon P values now include the executed shape factor max(1, rows/cols), checked against the fused step (tools/replay_equiv.py). Ratios moved 2–4%, κ .0430 → .0471 (spread 1.31 → 1.44), and no verdict changed.

R3, overclaims. §2/§4.2 no longer "rule out" the threshold of [7]. We test one timing reading, credit QAF to [7], and add Quartet II §§6.1–6.2 and Full-Stack FP4. "Thermal" is no longer asserted. Horizon claims are conditional (one seed, fitted curve, new data at 2×). The probe-underpricing factor is corrected from 5× to about 4×. A new §4.6 adds q23 (small batch; dose check failed, so descriptive).

R4, provenance. The supplement now has provenance/ (INDEX.md): data manifests pinned to HF revision 915333b4 with upstream SHA-256, the 31 held-out overlap hashes and scripts, the 2× data manifest, and a dated export of all 49 preregistration comments. §6 adds manipulation checks, AdamW warmup, shape factor and q23 limits.
title: What a Low-Precision Backward Pass Costs Muon: Phase, Horizon, Noise Structure, and an Unestablished Optimizer Contrast
